name: Old Meeting House
text: The Old Meeting House was constructed in Marblehead, Massachusetts in 1696 on Franklin Street. It was the second meeting house to be constructed for what would become the Congregationalist church. Portions of the meeting house pews are the largest group of joined interior paneling to survive from any seventeenth century New England Building, which still survive to this day in museums and private homes.

depictions.name: Old Meeting House
depictions.text: The Old Meeting House was a church located in Boston, Massachusetts. The church was significant for its bells which rang in the hours leading up to the Boston Massacre on 5 March 1770.
